products.overview: Industrial preparative chromatographs aren't off-the-shelf equipment. Each one is tailored to the user's specific separation, pressure, and throughput requirements. Separsys HP systems are industrial units for high-efficiency, high-pressure isocratic preparative chromatography, built for production-scale purification. The three configurations shown here, HP 400, 800 FP, and 300 DS, represent examples of systems already delivered to customers, each built around a different column size, pressure range, and pump configuration. Every system is fully controlled through modified ECOMAC software, and Inkarp's specialists work directly with you to develop the right specification for your process.
features: High-Pressure Column Design: Column pressure ratings from 50 to 100 bar depending on configuration, built for demanding industrial separations.
Modified ECOMAC Software Control: Sets separation parameters and monitors detector signal and column pressure from a single PC across all three systems.
Consistent Detection Architecture: PLCC 15 Ex detector cell paired with a FLASH 06S DAD 600 EX detector across the range.
Multi-Pump Mobile Phase Management: Hydracell membrane pumps handle mobile phase delivery, sample injection, and, where needed, piston actuation.
Centralized Pump Control: Remote switchboard with ABB frequency converters manages flow changes across pump motors.
Dedicated Hydraulic Piston System (300 DS): Separpress D100 EE 1300 delivers 100 tons of force across a full 1300mm piston stroke.
Automatic Bypass Detection (800 FP and 300 DS): Separpass 03 connects the detector cell to the column output from a 10-meter distance.
ATEX and Pressure Certification on Request: All industrial systems can be delivered with ATEX certification for hazardous environments and pressure certification for columns and the full system.

faqs.question: Can the Separsys HP systems be certified for hazardous environments?

faqs.question: Is pressure certification available for these systems?

faqs.question: What detector do the Separsys HP systems use?
faqs.answer: All three configurations use a PLCC 15 Ex detector cell paired with a FLASH 06S DAD 600 EX detector, connected directly or through an automatic bypass system depending on the configuration.

sections.title: Separsys HP Systems at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate the Separsys HP range: how HP 400, 800 FP, and 300 DS differ in column and pump design, shared control architecture, and Inkarp installation and service support.
sections.subheading: Industrial-scale preparative chromatography, built to your production needs.
body: All three systems are built for isocratic, high pressure, high performance preparative chromatography at industrial scale.
Each is fully controlled through modified ECOMAC software, which sets separation parameters and monitors both detector signal and column pressure from a single PC.
HP 400 runs a 399mm ID, 1000mm long column packed with 15 µm spherical silica using a sedimentation packing procedure, at up to 80 bar.
800 FP steps up in column diameter to 799mm, at up to 50 bar, and adds a special floating piston along with an automatic bypass detection system, Separpass 03, positioned 10 meters from the column.

300 DS uses a narrower 299mm ID but a longer 1300mm column with full-length piston stroke, packed with finer 10 µm silica by a dynamic slurry method, running at up to 100 bar, the highest pressure rating of the three.

300 DS is the only configuration built with its own dedicated hydraulic system, a Separpress D100 EE 1300 rated for 100 tons of force and 1300mm of stroke, alongside a flow reversion block that lets flow direction in the column be changed.
Every system uses multiple Hydracell membrane pumps working together to handle mobile phase delivery, sample injection, and, on 800 FP and 300 DS, additional roles like piston actuation.
Pump motors across all three systems are powered through a remote switchboard using ABB frequency converters, allowing flow changes to be managed centrally.

Because these are examples of already-delivered units rather than fixed catalog products, Inkarp recommends working directly with ECOM's specialists to develop the right specification for your process.

sections.title: System Architecture and Pump Configuration
body: Each Separsys system routes mobile phase, sample, and pressure control a little differently, shaped by its column size and target application.

On HP 400, three Hydracell P3 pumps split the work cleanly: two run in parallel to supply the mobile phase, while the third delivers the sample mixture to be separated, all monitored through electronic pressure sensors on the delivery block. 800 FP scales that up, pairing a higher-capacity Hydracell G10 pump for mobile phase supply with multiple G3 pumps handling sample injection and, notably, moving the column's floating piston, all routed through air-controlled ball valves rather than manual ones. 300 DS takes a different approach entirely, using two Hydracell G04 pumps rated for higher pressure (120 bar each) to handle mobile phase and sample together, while a separate, purpose-built Separpress hydraulic system handles the piston stroke across the column's full 1300mm length, an approach that also enables its dedicated flow reversion block.

Where site conditions call for it, all industrial systems can be delivered with ATEX certification for hazardous environments, and pressure certification for both the columns and the complete system, both available on request.
